subject: Hyperion Dedicated: memory pacing & KV-cache quantization — sizing ask
messages:
From: Amit Khurana <amit@hyperion.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@hyperion.ai
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing ask: model memory + KV-cache impact for Dedicated deal

Hey Markus —

Thanks for taking this. We're preparing the Dedicated commitment for our RAG/agent product and need a firm sizing recommendation that ties model memory + KV cache behavior to GPU counts. High level:
- Primary model: open-llama-70b (weight baseline) used for summarization + RAG answers.
- Secondary model: open-llama-13b (low-latency completion for UI microflows).
- Traffic expectations: peak 120 qps (spiky), sustained 50 qps; typical batch sizes are small (1–4).
- Context patterns: many sessions use long-context retrieval — average input tokens 1k, 95th percentile 8k; we plan to support up to 12k in some flows.
- Concurrency: roughly 50 concurrent user sessions during peak.

Questions:
1) For the 70B model, what is the per-replica GPU memory footprint in fp16 vs 4-bit quant (q4_0)? Include KV-cache sizing for long context (8k tokens) and an estimate per concurrent session.
2) If we enable CPU-hosted KV (offload) what latency hit should we expect at p95? Is that viable for our UX?
3) Recommendation for initial Dedicated commit (GPU type + count) and an autoscale burst strategy tied to the deal (we want a predictable monthly reserved cost but the ability to burst).
4) Any short-term knobs (batching, prefix caching, KV eviction) we should enable to reduce required GPUs without hurting UX significantly?

Attach: I can share our access patterns if it helps — sending a small sample separately.

Appreciate a concise recommendation + the primary tradeoffs. Procurement will need an SOW once we align.

— Amit
Amit Khurana
Head of Platform
Hyperion Therapeutics

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Amit Khurana <amit@hyperion.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-16T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: model memory + KV-cache impact for Dedicated deal

Amit — thanks for the clear brief. Below is a concise sizing response + tradeoffs. I kept the math at a high level so procurement can review with you; we can follow up with a detailed breakdown CSV (attached) for the SOW.

Short answer / recommendation
- Initial Dedicated commit: 8x H100-80GB GPUs reserved (two 4-GPU shards) with an autoscale policy to burst up to 32 GPUs across the pool. This gives predictable reserved capacity for your steady state (50 qps) and headroom for spikes while keeping per-month cost reasonable.
- Canary approach: start with q4 quantized replicas for the 70B to validate accuracy; keep one fp16 replica for latency-sensitive flows. If quality is acceptable we can move primary traffic to q4 and reduce sustained GPU needs by ~45–55%.

Key numbers & rationale (rough estimates, see attached CSV for line items)
- 70B baseline (fp16 weights): ~140 GB model weight resident memory (70B * 2 bytes). That generally maps to a 2–4 GPU model-parallel setup depending on GPU type and runtime sharding. With an H100-80GB we target 4 GPUs per replica to keep single-stream latency lower.
- 70B q4_0: quantized weight disk ~35–40 GB equivalent in GPU memory after packing/overheads — often allows 1–2 GPUs per replica. That reduces the weight footprint substantially, but KV-cache remains the dominant runtime working set for long context.
- KV-cache sizing: KV cache scales with sequence length and head/key size. Practical rule-of-thumb for our runtime: per-token KV bytes ~= 0.18–0.25 KB per token for wide attention models. At 8k context that is ~1.5–2.0 GB per concurrent request for 70B-class attention state. For 50 concurrent sessions that becomes untenable if stored fully on GPU (50 * 1.8GB ~= 90GB extra).
- Impact: quant reduces model weight footprint but KV cache overhead stays and can dominate memory at high concurrency for long contexts.

Offload options and UX tradeoffs
- Host (CPU) KV offload (we call this "memory pacing"): we page older KV blocks to host RAM and fetch on demand. Savings: reduces per-GPU GPU-RAM KV requirement by ~6–10 GB per active shard for high-context workloads. Latency: adds tail-latency at p95/p99 depending on host interconnect — expect ~15–35ms p95 extra in our tests, sometimes higher on cold pulls. For many RAG sessions this is acceptable; for low-latency UI microflows it's borderline.
- NVMe caching / burst buffer: we can add an NVMe tier for very large contexts (e.g., 100k) — this saves GPU RAM but can add 50–150ms on cold fetches. Better for async batch jobs than interactive UI.

Operational recommendation (deal-aligned)
- Reserved commit: 8 H100s (two 4-GPU replicas) for 3 months. Use q4 canary on 70B and run traffic split 10/90 (q4/fp16) to benchmark quality. If q4 passes, convert replicas to q4 and re-evaluate reserved quantity.
- Autoscale policy: allow bursting to 32 GPUs (soft cap) for daytime spikes; enforce per-model routing so microflow traffic prefers the 13B fp16 replicas.
- Immediate knobs: enable prefix caching for common system prompts and 2-minute KV eviction for inactive sessions to cap GPU KV growth. These lower the working set meaningfully with minimal UX impact.

I'll attach the CSV memory_breakdown. Marissa — please add anything on batching and runtime optimizations that can reduce GPUs without affecting p95. Rishi / Laura — procurement asks below.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Field Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sizing ask: model memory + KV-cache impact for Dedicated deal

Adding a few practical runtime points from ops / serving side:

- Continuous batching: because your qps is spiky, enabling continuous batching with small max-latency buckets (10–25ms) recovers throughput without much p95 impact and reduces per-token compute cost — this helps when we need to drop to fewer GPUs.
- Prefix/KV warm caches: we recommend pre-warming KV cache for your top ~20 system prompts (saves ~20–30% of active KV for demos/typical flows).
- KV eviction policy: 2-minute TTL for user sessions and aggressive eviction for sessions idle >30s reduces sustained KV retention. Combine with session affinity so a user's hot KV stays on the same shard for short durations.
- CPU-offload: when we enable host-KV offload we run a background compaction every 30s to reduce page churn. In our internal tests that keeps p95 delta low for typical RAG queries (<25ms) but p99s can spike — plan for that in SLOs.

Attachment: hyperion_kv_memory_breakdown.csv (per-model rows, per-token KV bytes, example concurrency scenarios).

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Amit / procurement —

We can do all three asks. Attached is a short SOW draft (hyperion_sow_draft.pdf) and a concise cost line:
- Reserved: 8x H100-80GB (3-month term) — estimated $XX,XXX / month (placeholder, will provide exact priced quote via sales contract).
- Burst policy: soft autoscale to 32 GPUs across the pool (burst billed at on-demand rates above reserved commit).
- Canary: 2 quantized (q4_0) replicas + 1 fp16 replica; traffic split 10% q4 / 90% fp16 for the first 48 hours, then expand q4 if accuracy is within agreed guardrails. Rapid rollback path to fp16 will be available via routing policy (under 5 minutes).
- Compliance: Dedicated in US region with SOC2 controls and customer-managed keys supported — we'll include the SOC2 addendum and network isolation language in the SOW.

Next steps:
1) Procurement: confirm you want a 3-month reserved term and give the billing contact. Rishi / Laura — can you prepare the formal quote + SOW with exact prices and attach the SOC2 attestation?
2) Ops: Marissa will run a q4/FP16 canary slot starting next Tue; Amit please provide the sample traffic logs you mentioned to seed prefix caches.

I'll follow up with the quote and final SOW PDF first thing tomorrow.
